nodes.summary: Evaluation depends only on variables that occur in the word.

nodes.summary: Removing unused images does not change the evaluated word.
nodes.title: Normalization does not change the evaluated word

nodes.summary: The embedding preserves substitution semantics.
nodes.title: Word embedding preserves substitution semantics

nodes.summary: Substitute words for variables in a word over constants and variables.
nodes.title: Substitution of words for variables in a word

nodes.summary: The ground test agrees with satisfaction under any substitution.
nodes.title: Ground test agrees with satisfaction under any substitution

nodes.summary: The executable ground test decides existence of a solution, not just satisfaction of one guessed substitution.
nodes.title: Ground test decides solvability of ground word equations

nodes.title: Executable satisfaction test for ground word equations

nodes.summary: Each occurring variable contributes a contiguous block, so its length cannot exceed the length of the evaluated word, even when substitutions may be empty.
nodes.title: Occurring variable's image is no longer than the evaluated word

nodes.summary: After normalization, every variable image, including unused ones, is bounded by the length of the original evaluation.
nodes.title: Normalized images are bounded by the evaluation length

nodes.summary: Normalization preserves the image of every occurring variable.
nodes.title: Normalization keeps images of occurring variables

nodes.summary: Every variable absent from the word has empty normalized image.
nodes.title: Normalization empties images of absent variables

nodes.summary: Retain the images of occurring variables and replace every unused image by `[]`. Only equality of variables, not equality of alphabet symbols, is needed.
nodes.title: Word substitution normalized by emptying unused images

nodes.summary: Matching a pattern against a fixed target loses no solutions by bounding ALL variable images by the target length. Unused variables are normalized to `[]`; an arbitrary unnormalized solution need not obey this bound.
nodes.title: Bounding variable images by the target loses no pattern matches

nodes.summary: The formula embedding preserves satisfaction.
nodes.title: Formula embedding of word equations preserves satisfaction

nodes.summary: An equation over `Fin n` is satisfiable iff it is satisfiable at some finite global length bound. There is no equation-computable bound claimed.

nodes.summary: An ordinary word equation, with no morphisms or language-membership atoms.
nodes.title: Ordinary word equation

nodes.summary: A system over finitely many variables has a solution iff one substitution solves every equation at some finite global length bound. The witness bound is obtained from the solution; this supplies no terminating general UNSAT test.
nodes.title: Solvability of word equation systems at a finite length bound

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
